plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value. However, a slight underbid is optimal to account for the fact that we pay the *second* highest bid. Since values are between 0 and 49, and my value is 32, I will bid slightly below this. I will bid 31.5 to attempt to win while minimizing the payment.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between 0 and 49, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately (2/3) * 49 = 32.67. To win reliably without overpaying, I'll bid slightly above this. However, my value is only 6, so I need to be very conservative. Bidding just above the expected second highest bid is too risky given my low value. A bid of 6.1 ensures I only win if another bidder drastically overestimates their value.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any deviation from your true value can be exploited by other rational bidders. If you bid below your value, you might lose the auction to someone who values the item more, even if their bid is only slightly above yours. If you bid above your value, you risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to you. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $17.
